evidence.claim: The World Bank approved a US$700 million operation tied to policies to simplify the business environment for small firms, promote financial inclusion, strengthen sustainable economic management, and expand support for vulnerable groups, rural areas, migrants, and women.
evidence.title: The World Bank and Mexico work together to foster inclusive and sustainable economic growth
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank approved a US$700 million operation tied to policies to simplify the business environment for small firms, promote financial inclusion, strengthen sustainable economic management, and expand support for vulnerable groups, rural areas, migrants, and women.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official World Bank press release describing the policy package and the government actions it supports.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 policy support during AMLO's presidency.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Supports ruler-period policy aims and implementation conditions, but the World Bank describes government policy actions rather than personal presidential execution in each detail.
contrary_evidence: The document is supportive and does not assess adverse side effects or implementation quality.
It is a policy-operation announcement, not an outcome evaluation.

evidence.claim: BBVA Research summarized Coneval's 2022 measurement, saying 46.8 million people were in poverty and 9.1 million in extreme poverty, while access to health worsened between 2018 and 2022.
evidence.title: Mexico | Poverty decreases at its lowest level (36.3%); but, access to health deteriorates
evidence.excerpt: BBVA Research summarized Coneval's 2022 measurement, saying 46.8 million people were in poverty and 9.1 million in extreme poverty, while access to health worsened between 2018 and 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent research summary of the official poverty measurement with explicit 2022 numbers.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on 2022 household welfare and distribution.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Only partly attributable to AMLO; the results reflect labor-market, social-policy, and structural factors over several years.
contrary_evidence: Health access deterioration is a significant negative offset.
Extreme poverty did not improve as strongly as headline poverty.

evidence.claim: The federal government issued a mandatory Program Estratégico de Salud para el Bienestar that aims to guarantee progressive, free, integral health services for people without social security and to strengthen federalization of health services.
evidence.title: ACUERDO por el que se emite el Programa Estratégico de Salud para el Bienestar
evidence.publisher: Diario Oficial de la Federación / Secretaría de Salud
evidence.excerpt: The federal government issued a mandatory Program Estratégico de Salud para el Bienestar that aims to guarantee progressive, free, integral health services for people without social security and to strengthen federalization of health services.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official legal instrument with explicit obligations, coverage aims, and federalization language.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 policy design and implementation framework.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's government through the federal health secretariat and the national plan it cites.
contrary_evidence: This is a program order, not proof of achieved outcomes.
It does not by itself show service quality or equal access across regions.

evidence.claim: The SEP said 2022 education programs received higher budgets, including La Escuela es Nuestra up 13.7 percent, Benito Juárez scholarships up 4 percent, special education funding up 1,134 percent, and textbook funding increased, alongside measures to reduce dropout.
evidence.title: Boletín SEP no. 24 Reciben programas educativos incremento presupuestal para 2022: Delfina Gómez Álvarez
evidence.publisher: Secretaría de Educación Pública, Gobierno de México
evidence.excerpt: The SEP said 2022 education programs received higher budgets, including La Escuela es Nuestra up 13.7 percent, Benito Juárez scholarships up 4 percent, special education funding up 1,134 percent, and textbook funding increased, alongside measures to reduce dropout.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct ministry budget announcement with program-specific figures and stated policy purpose.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 budget and delivery planning evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to AMLO's government through the education ministry and federal budget process.
contrary_evidence: Budget increases do not ensure effective delivery or learning gains.
The source is self-reported and policy-oriented.

evidence.claim: SEP and state education authorities launched a national re-enrollment and learning-recovery effort, including diagnostic evaluations in September 2022 and February 2023 to measure student progress and guide recovery actions.
evidence.title: Boletín SEP no 147 Convocatoria Nacional 'Vamos todas y todos por la educación' para la reinserción escolar y recuperación de aprendizajes
evidence.publisher: Secretaría de Educación Pública, Gobierno de México
evidence.excerpt: SEP and state education authorities launched a national re-enrollment and learning-recovery effort, including diagnostic evaluations in September 2022 and February 2023 to measure student progress and guide recovery actions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous ministry announcement with concrete diagnostic dates and recovery measures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to AMLO's government through SEP and national education coordination, though implementation depended on states and schools.
contrary_evidence: The initiative addresses pandemic damage; it does not prove preexisting learning loss was fully reversed.
Diagnostic tests show measurement, not outcomes.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said Mexico's Ministry of Education, with UNICEF and partners, used government-led Learning Camps to close foundational learning gaps, reaching thousands of children with targeted literacy and numeracy instruction and showing measurable gains in weeks.
evidence.title: Teaching at the Right Level supports learning recovery in Mexico
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said Mexico's Ministry of Education, with UNICEF and partners, used government-led Learning Camps to close foundational learning gaps, reaching thousands of children with targeted literacy and numeracy instruction and showing measurable gains in weeks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent UN agency case study describing a government-led intervention and its measured short-run effects.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 education-recovery evidence within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to AMLO's administration because the Ministry of Education led the initiative, though UNICEF and partners contributed materially.
contrary_evidence: This is a case study, not a national evaluation.
The evidence is strongest for targeted pilots, not universal coverage.

evidence.claim: AMLO said 25 million families would receive direct benefits in 2022, equal to about 70 percent of Mexican families, and that the poorest states were already being covered at 100 percent of households.
evidence.title: El 70% de las familias son beneficiarias de al menos uno de los Programas para el Bienestar
evidence.publisher: Programas para el Bienestar / Gobierno de México
evidence.excerpt: AMLO said 25 million families would receive direct benefits in 2022, equal to about 70 percent of Mexican families, and that the poorest states were already being covered at 100 percent of households.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential remarks published on the government welfare portal with specific coverage claims.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO, who publicly presented the distribution and coverage claims.
contrary_evidence: The claims are self-reported and do not prove outcomes or absence of exclusion.
Universal coverage in poor states is not the same as equal quality or adequacy of support.

evidence.claim: In 2022 Mexico's disability pension reached 1,301,922 people with 22 billion pesos of social investment, was universal in 14 states, and included rehabilitation support for more than 21,000 children.
evidence.title: 1.3 millones de personas ya reciben Pensión para el Bienestar de las Personas con Discapacidad, con inversión de 22 mil mdp
evidence.publisher: Secretaría de Bienestar, Gobierno de México
evidence.excerpt: In 2022 Mexico's disability pension reached 1,301,922 people with 22 billion pesos of social investment, was universal in 14 states, and included rehabilitation support for more than 21,000 children.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct ministry report with explicit beneficiary and financing figures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to AMLO's administration through national and state welfare financing.
contrary_evidence: The report is official and supportive; independent verification of outcomes is still needed.
Universal coverage was still limited to 14 states, so coverage was not nationwide.

evidence.claim: The welfare ministry said more than 11 million people and their families, including indigenous and afromexican communities, were directly benefited in 2021 and that the programs would continue in 2022 with guaranteed budget.
evidence.title: Destina Bienestar en 2021 casi 200 mil mdp para atención de las personas más pobres y vulnerables
evidence.publisher: Secretaría de Bienestar, Gobierno de México
evidence.excerpt: The welfare ministry said more than 11 million people and their families, including indigenous and afromexican communities, were directly benefited in 2021 and that the programs would continue in 2022 with guaranteed budget.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry summary of program reach and target groups, with a clear bridge into 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Baseline-plus-continuation evidence relevant to the 2022 period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to AMLO's welfare architecture, though the figures are a 2021 tally carried into 2022.
contrary_evidence: This is a ministry self-report and a pre-2022 tally.
It describes reach, not quality or distributive sufficiency.

evidence.claim: The 2022 phase of the Tianguis del Bienestar delivered 7,735,039 new basic-need items to 272,882 families in Guerrero, Oaxaca, Chiapas, and Veracruz, including hurricane-affected communities and the poorest areas.
evidence.title: Concluye primera fase del Tianguis del Bienestar con 7.7 millones de bienes entregados a 272 mil familias
evidence.publisher: Secretaría de Seguridad y Protección Ciudadana, Gobierno de México
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 phase of the Tianguis del Bienestar delivered 7,735,039 new basic-need items to 272,882 families in Guerrero, Oaxaca, Chiapas, and Veracruz, including hurricane-affected communities and the poorest areas.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct government operational report with exact delivery figures and target geography.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to AMLO's government, involving federal security, customs, finance, and social agencies.
contrary_evidence: The program is redistributive relief, not a structural poverty solution.
It covers selected regions rather than the whole country.

evidence.claim: Mexico launched Bienpesca 2022 with more than 1,360 million pesos to benefit 189,000 fishers and aquaculture workers, paying each beneficiary 7,200 pesos directly and without intermediaries.
evidence.title: Gobierno de México inicia la entrega de apoyos Bienpesca 2022
evidence.publisher: Programas para el Bienestar / Gobierno de México
evidence.excerpt: Mexico launched Bienpesca 2022 with more than 1,360 million pesos to benefit 189,000 fishers and aquaculture workers, paying each beneficiary 7,200 pesos directly and without intermediaries.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Government welfare portal with explicit budget, beneficiary, and anti-intermediary language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to AMLO's government because the program is presented as a federal welfare policy under his administration.
contrary_evidence: This is a sector-specific transfer program, not a broad social-service overhaul.
The source is self-reported and does not test impacts on living standards.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 evidence on AMLO's personal control over civilian-nuclear safety appointments, regulatory discipline, or command-side decisions is thin.
There is no Mexico-originating war, proxy conflict, or coercive peace leverage in 2022, so the dossier is mostly diplomatic posture rather than operational conflict conduct.
Specific chain-of-command evidence for some police, military, and intelligence abuses remains incomplete, especially for local versus federal responsibility.
Some of the evidence about electoral reform and media pressure is rhetorical or journalistic rather than a direct legal finding of intent to entrench power.
The causal split between AMLO policy, inherited weakness, and global shocks is still only partially recoverable for 2022 poverty, inflation, and investment outcomes.
Independent post-launch quality and outcome audits for IMSS-Bienestar, education recovery, and related welfare programs are thinner than the rollout record.
Direct documentary evidence of personal enrichment, hidden financial benefit, or knowing approval of surveillance remains limited.
Durability and post-launch independent audits for AIFA, Dos Bocas, IMSS-Bienestar, and the education programs are thinner than the implementation record.
